answer: Tie the stake to the prize, not the identity. Before a jury verdict settles, the deciding quorum must escrow coin equal to V, the value a captured ruling would extract, posted openly like a beacon any peer can audit. If a later review overturns that verdict, the escrow burns. So an attacker may wander across a thousand throwaway keys, each a cheap relic, and still gain nothing: moving a decision worth V locks and forfeits at least V of real capital each try. The cost tracks the prize, never the headcount, so a clone army buys no discount and the raid never clears what it must spend to win.
